MEMORANDUM
  Agenda Item #: 5
  Meeting Date: July 28, 2020

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL MEMBERS

THRU:  LAURA GUGLIELMO, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  BRIANNA RINDGE, ACTING PLANNING AND BUILDING
  DIRECTOR

SUBJECT:  RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE PARKLANDS COMMITTEE
  FOR JULY 9, 2020

DATE:  JULY 28, 2020

ACTION REQUIRED  X  CONSENT  X  RECEIVE & FILE

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council approve the actions of the Parklands Committee
for the meeting of July 9, 2020.

Summary

In the Parklands Committee meeting of July 9, 2020, all five committee members were
present. A total of five applications were discussed: three for tree removals for view
purposes; one for landscaping in Parklands; and one for landscaping a public median. Item
#6, a staff report for ‘Landscape Design Standards for Public Spaces’ was presented for
future discussion.

Analysis and Findings

The City held a Parklands Committee meeting on July 9, 2020 and the Committee
recommended the following actions to be approved by the City Council.

  1. PC-536-20; Application to remove one Eucalyptus tree located in the Parklands
  adjacent to 565 Via Del Monte

  1
   Applicant: Mona Fortenberry, 3050 Delaware Avenue, Santa Monica, CA 90404

Staff introduced the item as a view restoration application. The Eucalyptus tree is below
the home at 565 Via Del Monte and behind the home at 376 Palos Verdes Drive West. The
Eucalyptus encroaches upon a portion of the coastline view and the Queen’s Necklace. The
view on either side of the tree is clear and panoramic. This large, old tree provides screening
and privacy for a number of homes on Palos Verdes Drive West and recreational value for
the adjacent parklands trail. The applicant requested removal but trimming would improve
the view and retain the privacy and amenities the tree provides. Staff received numerous
individual letters and nearly 100 signatures on a petition from impacted residents
supporting trimming, but not removal. Andrew Mactavish and Duncan Mactavish spoke
in opposition to the application as residents beneath the shade tree which also provides
privacy.

The applicant indicated that the scenic view of the Queen’s Necklace is significantly
blocked for her parents who have lived in their home for 50 years. The applicant understood
the lack of support from the neighborhood and indicated that trimming is acceptable, but
not as limited as the recommendation by the Urban Forester.

The Committee agreed that the tree impacts the view significantly and improvement is
appropriate. Most of the Committee members agreed that a balance is necessary to both
improve the view and retain the tree. One member supported removal and replacement with
a large specimen tree that would not impact the view in the future.

Vice Chair Richie-Bray motioned and Committee member McCabe seconded (4-1 in favor,
Groves dissenting) to recommend approval with modification to trim the tree to reduce the
density by 25%, reduce the height by 5-10 feet, and reduce the width by 10-15 feet in late
fall or the winter months, at the direction of the Urban Forester, with a no-fee permit after
the first trimming.

  2. PC-537-20; Application to annually top three Carob trees located in the parkways
  adjacent to 2213 and 2217 Via Acalones

  Applicant: Richard and Julie Sullivan, 2220 Via Acalones, Palos Verdes Estates,
  CA 90274

Staff introduced the view restoration application for approval to annually reduce the height
of three Carob trees on Via Acalones. The applicant requests to top two trees at 15 feet in
height at 2213 Via Acalones, which the previous owner has lowered to 15 feet for the last
20 years, plus one Carob tree at 20 feet at 2217 Via Acalones. In 2017, the City approved
two separate applications to top 10 Carob trees on Via Acalones and the applicant would
like to add three more to be topped at the same time. Staff received two letters of support
from neighbors on Via Acalones.

  2
 The applicant indicated that his request to top the trees would retain neighborhood
character and restore view as long as the two trees at 2213 Via Acalones were reduced to
the height that existed when they purchased their home.

All Committee members agreed with the request to top the trees and expressed the desire
to process this request quickly so that all Carob trees may be topped at the same time.

Committee member Cooper motioned and Vice Chair Richie-Bray seconded (5-0 in favor)
to recommend approval to annually top the three Carob trees located within the parkways
adjacent to 2213 and 2217 Via Acalones with a tree topping permit the first year and a no-
fee permit thereafter: the two Carob trees at 2213 Via Acalones shall be topped at 15 feet
above grade and the Carob tree at 2217 Via Acalones shall be topped at 20 feet above
grade.

  3. PC-538-20; Application to top or remove five trees located in the parkway adjacent
  to 709 Paseo Del Mar

  Applicant: Greg Geiger, 715 Paseo Del Mar, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced the view restoration application to top or remove five trees that encroach
upon the view from the applicant’s main viewing area. Staff identified the trees as one
Ficus that was part of a property line hedge, one newly planted Olive tree on the left side
of the driveway, two severely trimmed Carob trees framing the driveway, and one Aleppo
Pine at the far end of the parkway. All trees were trimmed without permits by the gardener
and all but the two Carob trees are unpermitted and nonconforming. The Carob tree was
once the designated street tree for Paseo Del Mar. The Aleppo pine is not visible from the
main viewing area.

The applicant indicated the reason he submitted the application is that he has experienced
a lack of cooperation with his neighbor when requesting trimming of either private or
public trees that encroach upon his view. The applicant’s representative, Charles Petersen,
indicated that the trees block the view, the trees are not the designated street tree, that Paseo
Del Mar is a view street, and that the trees should be removed and be replaced with the
Kentia palm (the designated street tree).

Andrew Shoop, representative for Katina Torino who resides at 709 Paseo Del Mar,
indicated the trees provide a visual barrier for privacy and screening from the surfers and
beach visitors who use the parkway to change clothing. Wade Welch, a resident from Via
Media, indicated that a consistent enforcement of the view policy was required for this
application.

The Committee agreed that all but the Aleppo pine encroach upon a significant view, do
not provide beauty for the neighborhood, and do not provide privacy for 709 Paseo Del
Mar.

  3
 Committee member Cooper motioned and Committee member Groves seconded (5-0 in
favor) to recommend approval to remove the two Carob trees, one Olive tree, and one Ficus
tree adjacent to 709 Paseo Del Mar according to the “Standard Conditions For Tree
Removal Approvals” and to require removal of all stumps and a $1,000 payment to the
Tree Bank.

  4. PC-539-20; Application to landscape a portion of Parklands with native plants
  adjacent to 1400 Chelsea Road

  Applicant: Jeff Jellison, 1400 Chelsea Road, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced the application for landscaping a portion of Parklands, as guided by
adopted Resolution No. R12-05, the Parklands Landscaping Policy. A previous application
from Jeff Jellison was submitted to remove one Chinese Flame tree and all non-native trees
and shrubs in this same portion of Parklands. At that meeting, the applicant’s
representative, Marlene Breene, indicated her client would like to restore the Parklands
after the invasive non-native plants are removed. Staff indicated this would be a second
step and an application to landscape Parklands and was not part of this application.

The proposed landscape plan adds 5,000-6,000 public square feet to the private area
adjacent to the driveway at 1400 Chelsea Road. The location of the driveway is 1.5 feet
from the property line which does not provide much opportunity for landscaping. A
property line wall for security is not proposed. A native garden, as a barrier to keep the
public from wandering onto private property, could beautify the Parklands if approvable
under the Parklands Landscaping Policy. The policy requires four factors to exist, similar
to a variance from the Planning Commission, including that the landscaping shall not
appear privately owned or create a barrier to the public.

Marlene Breene indicated that the landscaping would improve the appearance of the
Parklands, deter invasive weeds, provide erosion control, deter unwanted activities in
Parklands, and improve public safety. Marlene Breene also indicated the plan was within
Fire Department regulations for landscaping and would not appear private.

All Committee members agreed the landscape appeared private but struggled with the
normal weedy appearance of Parklands and desire to approve a plan which improves
Parklands with native plants. One member suggested reduction of the amount of species
and relocation of the plants in a more random fashion to blend into Parklands to reduce the
appearance of private ownership.

Vice Chair Richie-Bray motioned and Committee member Cooper seconded (5-0 in favor)
to continue the item to the next Parklands Committee meeting to allow the applicant to
revise the plan as directed by the Committee and re-submit without a fee.

  5. PC-540-20; Application to landscape the center median adjacent to City Hall with
  California friendly drought tolerant plants

  4
   Applicant: Palos Verdes Estates Foundation, PO Box 955, Palos Verdes Estates,
  CA 90274

Staff introduced the application to landscape the center median adjacent to City Hall by a
non-profit organization as an improvement to public land, guided by public works
standards for safety. Standards for design of public spaces are not established but safety
and maintainability are required. Important considerations include maintenance factors that
reduce cost to the City budget for landscape maintenance in the future, sustainability, and
compatibility with the general landscapes in the area.

The project will be funded by the Foundation with the exception of mulch and boulder
donations by the City amounting to a $4,400 expenditure of labor by the Streets and Parks
Department if approved. Total cost of the project is estimated at $60,000.

Karen Logan, representing the Foundation, indicated that the location was chosen as an
optimal place to start a collaborative beautification effort at the hub of the City for traffic
and business. The group make effort to choose colorful plants found in existing nearby
landscapes for compatibility and beauty. A clear area around the perimeter is included for
performance of maintenance activities without minimal traffic impact and worker safety.
Plants are restricted to 30” in height especially at intersections. Boulders are proposed to
add character no closer than 10 feet from the curb. An additional clear area of 10 feet is
provided on the side closest to City Hall for community activities involving street closure.

Chad MacAllister of the Malaga Cove Homeowner’s Association spoke in support of the
project and indicated more projects are in the planning phase for the future. Virginia Butler,
also of the Palos Verdes Estates Foundation, spoke in support of this project as well.

The Committee agreed this would be a good project and was much needed as the median
is unattractive in its present state. All members agreed the plans need to be modified but
could be approved conceptually to start preliminary preparations for watering and weed
removal. Vice Chair Richie-Bray suggested eliminating some of the out-of-character
succulents, adding more stately plants at the ends and highly visible areas, substituting one
grass verity with one currently in use in other areas for consistency, and providing larger
massing of plants to provide a more unified look from the street and a more lush, green
appearance. Creeping Shore Juniper, blue fescue and more blue chalk sticks for massing
along borders is suggested.

Committee member Cooper motioned and Committee member Groves seconded (5-0 in
favor) to recommend approval with modification of the conceptual plan, requiring that the
applicant re-submit a new plan incorporating the direction provided by the Parklands
Committee for consideration at the September Parklands Committee meeting. If the
conceptual plan is approved by the City Council, weed clearing may begin but planting
shall not commence until the Parklands Committee hears and the City Council approves
the final design.

  5
   6. Discussion to establish Landscape Design Standards for Public Spaces

Staff indicated this item is to provide the Committee, the community, and applicants a
better understanding of acceptable standards for landscaping, including design, on public
land throughout the city. The process of approving landscapes without clear guidelines may
create a patchwork of incohesive and out-of-character landscapes. Standards will simplify
the process and guide the Parklands Committee members in making decisions. Staff
recommends appointing an ad hoc committee to establish a policy for landscape design
standards for public spaces.

Vice Chair Richie-Bray motioned and Committee member Groves seconded (5-0 in favor)
to appoint Vice Chair Debra Richie-Bray and Committee member Jeff Groves to an ad hoc
committee to develop “Landscape Design Standards for Public Spaces”.

Notification

These matters have been agenized and posted in the routine manner.

Staff reported prepared by:
Carl Moritz
Urban Forester
